title: Duplicate names in JSON objects do not guarantee uniform results
summary: JSON recommends unique object member names. On duplicate keys, parsers may keep only the last value, keep all values, or report an error.
detail: If the original text is read directly into a dictionary that only holds unique keys, subsequent traversals may not see the original duplicates.
boundary: Escapes of object names are explained before comparison; different original spellings may represent the same name.
relevance: Explain why the two parsing tools give different field contents, or an item is lost after reserialization.
